explainer_reply:
The marked tokens are highly diverse with uniformly weak activations (mostly 2–4), but share a loose tendency: they often occur at the start of a new text segment — the opening of quoted dialogue (quotation marks, em-dashes in Russian dialogue), newlines, list items, or multiple-choice answer letters (A, B, C, D). Many examples also come from non-English text (Russian/Cyrillic, Chinese) or corrupted text containing replacement characters, and from structured formats like SQL dumps and exam questions.

[EXPLANATION]: Weak activation on tokens at segment boundaries — beginnings of quoted speech, new lines, list entries, or multiple-choice options — frequently within non-English (Cyrillic/Chinese), corrupted, or highly structured text.
